final_recommendation: The room converged on a highly structured, operationalized D&O/E&O underwriting framework with pooled audit-firm caps, mandatory compliance monitoring, correlated-failure sub-limits, and unified defense counsel—pricing at +35% with hard clawbacks and reporting triggers. Execution risk remains around automated compliance workflows and portfolio-wide auditor concentration.
minority_objections: AI agent analyst repeatedly flagged that automated compliance workflows could bypass human materiality review, allowing control deficiencies to be 'workflow-approved' before monitors see dissent
Reinsurance manager raised unresolved concern about scaling the pooled-cap framework portfolio-wide, creating systemic auditor-concentration risk
Emerging risk lead questioned whether social media/market chatter should trigger reporting (overruled by claims counsel as unenforceable)
key_conflicts: First-breach vs. aggregate-burn clawback structure (resolved in favor of first-breach with mandatory 48-hour reporting)
Formal regulatory triggers vs. social media awareness as reporting obligation (resolved: formal triggers only)
Whether monitor audits automated compliance workflows or only reviews human sign-offs (unresolved)
key_concessions: Financial lines underwriter accepted $2M per-account defense cost floor as sunk litigation cost, not insured obligation
Claims counsel conceded that social media triggers are unenforceable, limiting reporting to formal regulatory/media inquiries
D&O specialist accepted that audit-engagement independence verification is monitor's responsibility, not underwriter's pre-binding check
red_lines: No shared audit-testing engagements across pooled accounts—separate engagements mandatory or Deloitte excluded entirely
Risk-committee minutes showing documented dissent on material weaknesses must be filed 60 days before renewal—no exceptions
Auditor E&O tail minimum $100M per firm; below that triggers mandatory rotation or exclusion
24-hour correlated-failure reporting window is automatic warranty breach if missed
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Portfolio-wide auditor concentration if pooled-cap framework scales beyond three accounts
Automated compliance systems that pre-approve control findings before human materiality review
Speed of reputational contagion via social media (dismissed as unenforceable but not modeled as claims-acceleration factor)
Regulatory compression—no discussion of how short regulatory decision windows (48-72 hours in Credit Suisse) affect claims timing or insured's ability to comply with reporting SLAs
downstream_risk_variables: Pooled audit-firm cap (max 2-3 same-auditor accounts per portfolio)
Correlated control-failure sub-limit ($8M independent of aggregate cap)
Net retention structure ($15M per account, $35M aggregate)
Defense cost floor ($2M per account, tracked against six-year litigation tail)
Mandatory compliance monitor with audit-engagement independence verification
24-hour correlated-failure reporting window with automatic warranty breach
Regulatory/media inquiry triggers immediate cross-account reporting, bypassing 24-hour window
Auditor E&O tail minimum ($100M per firm)
uncertainty_notes: Unresolved: whether monitor must audit automated compliance workflows that pre-approve control findings; portfolio-wide cap on total same-auditor exposures if framework scales; enforceability of materiality pre-approval if insured's system batches findings before human review; speed of reputational contagion via social media (dismissed but not modeled as claims-timing variable).
